name: Musquash Root
summary: Musquash Root is a rare botanical specimen found only in the damp soil beneath the massive waterfalls of the Stonewrought Dam in the Wetlands. It serves as a vital component in a concoction brewed by cultists hidden beneath Stormwind.

sections.title: A Rare Ingredient
sections.body: Musquash Root thrives in the perpetually mist-soaked ground where the cascade of the Stonewrought Dam crashes into the Wetlands. Its secluded and damp habitat makes it exceedingly difficult to harvest. While ordinary herbalists rarely seek it out, certain practitioners of the darker arts value the root for its potent chemical and alchemical properties.

sections.title: The Warlock's Scheme
sections.body: Beneath the streets of Stormwind, in the shadowy underbelly known as the Slaughtered Lamb, Zardeth of the Black Claw seeks this root alongside the Tear of Tilloa. Together, these rare flora form the foundation of a subtle brew designed to neutralize Lord Wishock, a member of the House of Nobles who has begun poking his nose into the city's hidden coven of warlocks.

faq.answer: Musquash Root grows exclusively in the Wetlands, resting at the very foot of the great falls beneath the Stonewrought Dam.

faq.q: What is Musquash Root used for?
aliases: why do i need musquash root
faq.answer: Zardeth of the Black Claw requests it alongside the Tear of Tilloa for a brew intended to keep Lord Wishock preoccupied and halt his push for an investigation into Stormwind's warlock coven.
Zardeth of the Black Claw, a warlock residing in the catacombs beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, directs agents to retrieve it.
Lord Wishock is a member of Stormwind's House of Nobles who learned about the warlock coven operating within the city and began lobbying the council for a formal investigation.

angles.text: For warlocks operating beneath the Slaughtered Lamb, obtaining this root is essential to silencing nosy nobles and safeguarding their fragile sanctuary within the city.
Though not a standard trade herb, the root demonstrates how specific microclimates like the base of the Stonewrought Dam can nurture unique and dangerous flora.
